p: The Rural Life Living Museum sits in some of the loveliest countryside in Surrey, and it's easy to build a whole day around it. Tilford is a pretty village with a large green, two old bridges over the River Wey and a famous oak tree, and it's worth a short stroll before or after your visit. The surrounding heathland and woodland are perfect for walking, so bring boots if you fancy stretching your legs.

At the museum, it helps to plan around the volunteers. Many of the trades, from the blacksmith's forge to the woodyard, are demonstrated by enthusiasts who give up their time, so the best experiences often happen on event days when lots of demonstrators are about. The light railway is always popular with younger visitors, while older kids might enjoy the schoolroom and the old shops, where they can compare village life with their own.

A few miles away, Waverley Abbey is the ruin of the first Cistercian abbey in England, sitting beside the River Wey in a peaceful setting that's great for a picnic. Frensham Ponds, a pair of large lakes surrounded by heathland, is a favourite spot for walks, birdwatching and paddling on a hot day.

Farnham itself has a historic castle, a lively town centre with independent shops and cafés, and lovely Georgian streets. Alice Holt Forest, south-west of the town, has trails, play areas and a treetop adventure course for older kids. Mix and match these and you've got a weekend packed with fresh air and history, all within a short hop of the museum.
